newsitem.title: USA: TCI bond prices rise on S&P rating move.
newsitem.headline: TCI bond prices rise on S&P rating move.

text.p: Spreads on TCI Communications bonds tightened by 20 basis points in Friday morning trading on news that Standard & Poor's had affirmed the cable company's debt ratings.
"The market expected this to happen, but on good news, as with bad news, the market moves," said Marion Boucher Soper, cable and telecommunications analyst at Bear Stearns & Co Inc.

After a review which lasted over four months, S&P decided to affirm TCI's corporate credit rating at BBB-minus, the lowest level which is still considered investment grade. S&P's review, which began on October 10, 1996, threatened to lower the company's rating to junk bond status.

S&P stated on Friday, "The affirmation reflects S&P's belief that TCI's significant shift in capital spending strategy and shift to lower its operting cost structure will result in the company's meeting S&P's parameters for a marginal investment-grade rating over 1997."
"Clearly, the story turned the corner in late November becuase of (CEO John) Malone's renewed commitment to actively manage the company," said Boucher Soper.
"S&P is really saying that they believe that tha laundry list of reforms which Malone promised will come to fruition in the next six months," she added.

As of Friday morning, TCI's 7 7/8 percent bond of '13 which is considered a benchmark issue by some traders, was quoted at a spread of 168-163. Traders said the bonds were quoted 20 basis points wider as of market close on Thursday.
